text.p: Following are the main stories in Monday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said he was waiting for a full report from the Transport Ministry on reported problems affecting Malaysian Airlines. He was commenting on a newspaper report that the airline's services were on the decline.
-- Most credit and charge card issuers are believed to have not started collecting the 50 ringgit extra fee which the government proposed two months ago to dissuade card ownership.
-- Bus-maker Master-Builders (M) Sdn Bhd, an associate of DRB-Hicom, plans to increase its output of buses to meet local demand, said CEO Abdul Aziz Mohd.
-- About half of 35,567 hectraes of land gazetted as Kedah state's permanent forest reserve have been officially classified as "missing" -- sold or given away to certain parties.
